chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Imran al-Halabi, who said:

Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام was asked about a man who forgot to fast the three days that are due upon the mutamatti' when he does not find the sacrificial offering, until he returned to his family. He said: He should send a sacrificial blood-offering.

The proper way to understand this report is what we have already mentioned in the previous chapter: that he sends a blood-offering if Dhu al-Hijjah has passed and he did not fast. It is only permissible for him to fast the three days so long as he remains within Dhu al-Hijjah.

key_terms.ذُو ٱلْحِجَّةِ: the month during which this fasting remains valid
key_terms.يَبْعَثُ بِدَمٍ: he sends an animal for sacrifice as compensation
key_terms.يَصُومَ: to fast as an act of worship and legal obligation
key_terms.ٱلثَّلَاثَةَ ٱلْأَيَّامِ: the three obligatory days of fasting in place of the sacrificial offering
key_terms.ٱلْهَدْيَ: the sacrificial offering required in hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mutamatti' forgets to fast the three days in Dhu al-Hijjah and returns home?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling for a pilgrim performing tamattu' who failed to fast the three substitute days required when he could not find the sacrificial offering. It states that if Dhu al-Hijjah has passed without those fasts being observed, he must send a sacrificial offering instead, since the time for fasting those three days is limited to Dhu al-Hijjah.
